Main.sentence: The Democratic Party is a liberal ___E:political party in the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_parties_in_the_United_States)___ .

Sitting on the ___E:center U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centrism)___ to ___E:center-left U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centre-left_politics)___ of the political spectrum, it is the world's oldest active political party, having been founded in 1828. Its main rival is the ___E:Republican Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States))___ , and since the 1850s the two have since dominated ___E:American politics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_politics)___ .

It initially supported ___E:Jacksonian democracy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacksonian_democracy)___ , ___E:agrarianism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agrarianism)___ , and ___E:geographical expansionism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manifest_destiny)___ , while opposing ___E:a national bank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_War)___ and high ___E:tariffs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tariff)___ .
Democrats won six of the eight presidential elections from 1828 to 1856, losing twice to the ___E:Whigs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whig_Party_(United_States))___ .

In 1860, the party split into ___E:Northern U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Democrats)___ and ___E:Southern U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Democrats)___ factions over ___E:slavery U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slavery_in_the_United_States)___ .

The party remained dominated by agrarian interests, contrasting with Republican support for the ___E:big business U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_business)___ of the ___E:Gilded Age U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilded_Age)___ .

Democratic candidates won the presidency only twice [b] between 1860 and 1908 though they ___E:won the popular vote U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_presidential_elections_in_which_the_winner_lost_the_popular_vote)___ two more times in that period.

During the ___E:Progressive Era U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_Era)___ , some factions of the party supported ___E:progressive U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressivism_in_the_United_States)___ reforms, with ___E:Woodrow Wilson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodrow_Wilson)___ being elected president in 1912 and 1916.

In 1932, ___E:Franklin D. Roosevelt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin_D._Roosevelt)___ was elected president after campaigning on a strong response to the ___E:Great Depression U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression)___ .

His ___E:New Deal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Deal)___ programs created ___E:a broad Democratic coalition U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Deal_coalition)___ which united White southerners, Northern workers, ___E:labor unions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labor_unions_in_the_United_States)___ , ___E:African Americans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Americans)___ , ___E:Catholic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church_in_the_United_States)___ and ___E:Jewish communities U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Jews)___ , progressives, and ___E:liberals U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_liberalism_in_the_United_States)___ .

From the late 1930s, ___E:a conservative minority U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservative_coalition)___ in the party's Southern wing joined with Republicans to slow and stop further progressive domestic reforms.

After the ___E:civil rights movement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_rights_movement)___ and ___E:Great Society U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Society)___ era of progressive legislation under ___E:Lyndon B. Johnson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyndon_B._Johnson)___ , who was often able to overcome the conservative coalition in the 1960s, many White southerners ___E:switched to the Republican Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_strategy)___ as the Northeastern states became more reliably Democratic.

The party's labor union element has weakened since the 1970s amid ___E:deindustrialization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deindustrialization)___ , and during the 1980s it lost many White working-class voters to the Republicans under ___E:Ronald Reagan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan)___ .

The election of ___E:Bill Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton)___ in 1992 marked a shift for the party toward ___E:centrism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centrism)___ and the ___E:Third Way U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_Way)___ , shifting its economic stance toward ___E:market-based policies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neoliberalism)___ .    ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ oversaw the party's passage of the ___E:Affordable Care Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affordable_Care_Act)___ in 2010.

In the 21st century, the Democratic Party's strongest demographics are ___E:urban voters U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban%E2%80%93rural_political_divide)___ , ___E:college graduates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Educational_attainment_in_the_United_States)___ (especially those with ___E:graduate degrees U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Postgraduate_education)___ ), ___E:African Americans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Americans)___ , women, ___E:younger voters U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Youth_vote_in_the_United_States)___ , irreligious voters, the unmarried and ___E:LGBTQ people U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBTQ_people_in_the_United_States)___ .

On social issues, it advocates for ___E:abortion rights U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abortion-rights_movements)___ ,  ___E:gun control U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gun_control)___ ,  ___E:LGBTQ rights U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBTQ_rights_in_the_United_States)___ ,  action on ___E:climate change U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_change)___ ,  and the ___E:legalization of marijuana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legality_of_cannabis_by_U.S._jurisdiction)___ .

On economic issues, the party favors ___E:healthcare reform U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Healthcare_reform_in_the_United_States)___ , ___E:paid sick leave U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paid_sick_leave)___ , ___E:paid family leave U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paid_family_leave)___ and ___E:supporting unions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unionization)___ .

In foreign policy, the party supports ___E:liberal internationalism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberal_internationalism)___ as well as tough stances against ___E:China U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China)___ and ___E:Russia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia)___ .

Democratic Party officials often trace its origins to the ___E:Democratic-Republican Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic-Republican_Party)___ , founded by ___E:Thomas Jefferson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Jefferson)___ , ___E:James Madison U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Madison)___ and other influential opponents of the conservative ___E:Federalists U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federalist_Party)___ in 1792.   That party died out before the modern Democratic Party was organized;  the Jeffersonian party also inspired the ___E:Whigs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whig_Party_(United_States))___ and modern Republicans.

Historians argue that the modern Democratic Party was first organized in the late 1820s with the election of war hero ___E:Andrew Jackson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Jackson)___  of Tennessee, making it the world's oldest active political party.
It was predominately built by ___E:Martin Van Buren U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Van_Buren)___ , who assembled a wide cadre of politicians in every state behind Jackson.

Since the nomination of ___E:William Jennings Bryan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Jennings_Bryan)___ in 1896, the party has generally positioned itself to the left of the ___E:Republican Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States))___ on economic issues.
Democrats have been more liberal on civil rights since 1948, although conservative factions within the Democratic Party that opposed them persisted in the South until the 1960s.
On foreign policy, both parties have changed positions several times.

The Democratic Party evolved from the ___E:Jeffersonian Republican U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeffersonian_Republican)___ or ___E:Democratic-Republican Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic-Republican_Party)___ organized by Jefferson and Madison in opposition to the Federalist Party.

The Democratic-Republican Party favored ___E:republicanism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republicanism_in_the_United_States)___ , a weak ___E:federal government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government_of_the_United_States)___ , ___E:states' rights U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/States%27_rights)___ , agrarian interests (especially Southern planters), and strict adherence to the Constitution.
The party opposed a national bank and ___E:Great Britain U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Great_Britain)___ .

After the ___E:War of 1812 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_of_1812)___ , the Federalists virtually disappeared and the only national political party left was the Democratic-Republicans, which was prone to splinter along regional lines.

The era of one-party rule in the United States, known as the ___E:Era of Good Feelings U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Era_of_Good_Feelings)___ , lasted from 1816 until 1828, when Andrew Jackson became president.
Jackson and Martin Van Buren worked with allies in each state to form a new Democratic Party on a national basis.
In the 1830s, the ___E:Whig Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whig_Party_(United_States))___ coalesced into the main rival to the Democrats.

When exactly the Democratic party formed is still debated among historians, with many putting forth the 1828 date of the creation of a federal structure for the various Jacksonian movements as the foundation date, however, it could also be argued that the foundation of these Jacksonian groups could be the foundation date. In that case the Democratic Party would be formed on December 23, 1823 when the Greensburg Committee read the Greensburg Resolution outside the ___E:Westmoreland County Courthouse U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westmoreland_County_Courthouse)___ in ___E:Greensburg, Pennsylvania U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greensburg,_Pennsylvania)___ .

The committee consisted of five of Greensburg's most prominent political figures, the brothers ___E:Jacob M. Wise U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacob_M._Wise)___ (state senator), ___E:John H. Wise U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_H._Wise_(Pennsylvania_politician))___ (state representative and brigadier general), and Frederick A. Wise (owner and editor of the Westmoreland Republican ), alongside ___E:David Marchand U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Marchand)___ (state representative), and ___E:James Clarke U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Clarke_(Pennsylvania_politician))___ (state representative).

The Greensburg Resolution was the first published call for Jackson to run for President with the committee being the first overtly "Jacksonian" organization, dubbed the 'origin' of the Jackson movement that turned into the Democratic party.

The event that transformed the Jacksonians from just another faction of the Democratic-Republican party into a divergent political force would be the so-called " ___E:corrupt bargain U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corrupt_bargain)___ " of 1824, where, despite winning the most popular and electoral votes, the House of Representatives did not confirm Jackson as the newly elected president, instead ___E:Henry Clay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay)___ , who was both a candidate and the speaker of the house, ___E:whipped U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whip_(politics))___ his supporters in congress to vote for the runner-up, ___E:John Quincy Adams U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Quincy_Adams)___ , in exchange for Adams naming Clay the Secretary of State.
Jackson and his followers began to more seriously coalesce into a structured party for the next election in 1828.

Before 1860, the Democratic Party supported ___E:expansive presidential power U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unitary_executive_theory)___ ,  ___E:the interests U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slave_Power)___ of ___E:slave states U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slave_states_and_free_states)___ ,  ___E:agrarianism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agrarianism)___ ,  and ___E:expansionism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expansionism)___ ,  while opposing ___E:a national bank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_War)___ and high ___E:tariffs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tariff)___ .

The ___E:Democratic-Republican Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic-Republican_Party)___ split over the choice of a successor to President ___E:James Monroe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Monroe)___ .

The faction that supported many of the old ___E:Jeffersonian principles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeffersonian_democracy)___ , led by Andrew Jackson and Martin Van Buren, became the modern Democratic Party.

Historian ___E:Mary Beth Norton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Beth_Norton)___ explains the transformation in 1828: .mw-parser-output .templatequote{overflow:hidden;margin:1em 0;padding:0 32px}.mw-parser-output .templatequotecite{line-height:1.5em;text-align:left;margin-top:0}@media(min-width:500px){.mw-parser-output .templatequotecite{padding-left:1.6em}}
Jacksonians believed the people's will had finally prevailed.
Through a lavishly financed coalition of state parties, political leaders, and newspaper editors, a popular movement had elected the president.
The Democrats became the nation's first well-organized national party ... and tight party organization became the hallmark of nineteenth-century American politics.
Behind the platforms issued by state and national parties stood a widely shared political outlook that characterized the Democrats:
The Democrats represented a wide range of views but shared a fundamental commitment to the Jeffersonian concept of an agrarian society.
They viewed the central government as the enemy of individual liberty.
The ___E:1824 "corrupt bargain" U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corrupt_bargain#Election_of_1824)___ had strengthened their suspicion of Washington politics. ...
Jacksonians feared the concentration of economic and political power.

They believed that government intervention in the economy benefited special-interest groups and created corporate monopolies that favored the rich. They sought to restore the independence of the individual—the artisan and the ordinary farmer—by ending federal support of banks and corporations and restricting the use of paper currency, which they distrusted.

Their definition of the proper role of government tended to be negative, and Jackson's political power was largely expressed in negative acts. He exercised the veto more than all previous presidents combined. ...
Nor did Jackson share reformers' humanitarian concerns.
He had no sympathy for American Indians, initiating the removal of the Cherokees along the ___E:Trail of Tears U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trail_of_Tears)___ .
Opposing factions led by ___E:Henry Clay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay)___ helped form the Whig Party.
The Democratic Party had a small yet decisive advantage over the Whigs until the 1850s when the Whigs fell apart over the issue of slavery.

In 1854, angry with the ___E:Kansas–Nebraska Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas%E2%80%93Nebraska_Act)___ , anti-slavery Democrats left the party and joined Northern Whigs to form the ___E:Republican Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_United_States_Republican_Party)___ .

Martin van Buren also helped found the ___E:Free Soil Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_Soil_Party)___ to oppose the spread of slavery, running as its candidate in the ___E:1848 presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1848_United_States_presidential_election)___ , before returning to the Democratic Party and staying loyal to the Union.

The Democrats split over slavery, with Northern and Southern tickets in the ___E:election of 1860 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1860_United_States_presidential_election)___ , in which the Republican Party gained ascendancy.

The radical pro-slavery ___E:Fire-Eaters U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fire-Eaters)___ led walkouts at the two conventions when the delegates would not adopt a resolution supporting the extension of slavery into territories even if the voters of those territories did not want it. These ___E:Southern Democrats U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1860_United_States_presidential_election#Constitutional_(Southern)_Democratic)___ nominated the pro-slavery incumbent vice president, ___E:John C. Breckinridge U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_C._Breckinridge)___ of Kentucky, for president and General ___E:Joseph Lane U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Lane)___ , of Oregon, for vice president.

The ___E:Northern Democrats U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1860_United_States_presidential_election#National_(Northern)_Democratic)___ nominated Senator ___E:Stephen A. Douglas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_A._Douglas)___ of Illinois for president and former Georgia Governor ___E:Herschel V. Johnson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herschel_Vespasian_Johnson)___ for vice president.
This fracturing of the Democrats led to a Republican victory and ___E:Abraham Lincoln U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Lincoln)___ was elected the 16th president of the United States.

As the ___E:American Civil War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Civil_War)___ broke out, Northern Democrats were divided into ___E:War Democrats U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_Democrats)___ and ___E:Peace Democrats U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copperheads_(politics))___ .
The ___E:Confederate States of America U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confederate_States_of_America)___ deliberately avoided organized political parties.

Most War Democrats rallied to Republican President Abraham Lincoln and the Republicans' ___E:National Union Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Union_Party_(United_States))___ in the ___E:election of 1864 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1864_United_States_presidential_election)___ , which featured ___E:Andrew Johnson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Johnson)___ on the Union ticket to attract fellow Democrats.
Johnson replaced Lincoln in 1865, but he stayed independent of both parties.

The Democrats benefited from white Southerners' resentment of ___E:Reconstruction U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reconstruction_era_of_the_United_States)___ after the war and consequent hostility to the Republican Party.

After ___E:Redeemers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redeemers)___ ended Reconstruction in the 1870s and following the often extremely violent ___E:disenfranchisement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disenfranchisement_after_the_Reconstruction_Era)___ of African Americans led by such ___E:white supremacist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_supremacy#Academic_use_of_the_term)___ Democratic politicians as ___E:Benjamin Tillman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Tillman)___ of ___E:South Carolina U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Carolina)___ in the 1880s and 1890s, the South, voting Democratic, became known as the " ___E:Solid South U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solid_South)___ ".
Although Republicans won all but two presidential elections, the Democrats remained competitive.

The party was dominated by pro-business ___E:Bourbon Democrats U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bourbon_Democrat)___ led by ___E:Samuel J. Tilden U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_J._Tilden)___ and ___E:Grover Cleveland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grover_Cleveland)___ , who represented mercantile, banking, and railroad interests; opposed ___E:imperialism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperialism)___ and overseas expansion; fought for the ___E:gold standard U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_standard)___ ; opposed ___E:bimetallism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bimetallism)___ ; and crusaded against corruption, high taxes and tariffs.

Cleveland was elected to non-consecutive presidential terms in ___E:1884 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1884_United_States_presidential_election)___ and ___E:1892 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1892_United_States_presidential_election)___ .

Agrarian Democrats demanding ___E:free silver U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_silver)___ , drawing on Populist ideas, overthrew the Bourbon Democrats in 1896 and nominated ___E:William Jennings Bryan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Jennings_Bryan)___ for the presidency (a nomination repeated by Democrats in 1900 and 1908).
Bryan waged a vigorous campaign attacking Eastern moneyed interests, but he lost to Republican ___E:William McKinley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_McKinley)___ .

The Democrats took control of the House in 1910, and ___E:Woodrow Wilson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodrow_Wilson)___ won election as president in 1912 (when the Republicans split) and 1916. Wilson effectively led Congress to put to rest the issues of tariffs, money, and antitrust, which had dominated politics for 40 years, with new progressive laws. He failed to secure Senate passage of the ___E:Versailles Treaty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Versailles_Treaty)___ (ending the war with Germany and joining the League of Nations).
The weakened party was deeply divided by issues such as the KKK and prohibition in the 1920s.
However, it did organize new ethnic voters in Northern cities.

After ___E:World War I U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I)___ ended and continuing through the ___E:Great Depression U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression)___ , the Democratic and Republican Parties both largely believed in ___E:American exceptionalism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_exceptionalism)___ over European monarchies and ___E:state socialism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_socialism)___ that existed elsewhere in the world.

The ___E:Great Depression U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression)___ in 1929 that began under Republican President ___E:Herbert Hoover U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbert_Hoover)___ and the Republican Congress set the stage for a more liberal government as the Democrats controlled the House of Representatives nearly uninterrupted from 1930 until 1994, the Senate for 44 of 48 years from 1930, and won most presidential elections until 1968. ___E:Franklin D. Roosevelt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin_D._Roosevelt)___ , elected to the presidency in 1932, came forth with federal government programs called the ___E:New Deal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Deal)___ .

New Deal liberalism meant the regulation of business (especially finance and banking) and the promotion of labor unions as well as federal spending to aid the unemployed, help distressed farmers and undertake large-scale public works projects.
It marked the start of the American welfare state.
The opponents, who stressed opposition to unions, support for business and low taxes, started calling themselves "conservatives".

Until the 1980s, the Democratic Party was a coalition of two parties divided by the Mason–Dixon line: liberal Democrats in the North and culturally conservative voters in the South, who though benefitting from many of the New Deal public works projects, opposed increasing ___E:civil rights U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_and_political_rights)___ initiatives advocated by northeastern liberals.

The polarization grew stronger after Roosevelt died. Southern Democrats formed a key part of the bipartisan ___E:conservative coalition U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservative_coalition)___ in an alliance with most of the Midwestern Republicans.

The economically activist philosophy of Franklin D. Roosevelt, which has strongly influenced ___E:American liberalism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberalism_in_the_United_States)___ , shaped much of the party's economic agenda after 1932.  From the 1930s to the mid-1960s, the liberal ___E:New Deal coalition U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Deal_coalition)___ usually controlled the presidency while the conservative coalition usually controlled Congress.

Issues facing parties and the United States after World War II included the ___E:Cold War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War)___ and the ___E:civil rights movement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_rights_movement)___ .

Republicans attracted conservatives and, after the 1960s, white Southerners from the Democratic coalition with their use of the ___E:Southern strategy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_strategy)___ and resistance to New Deal and ___E:Great Society U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Society)___ liberalism.
Until the 1950s, African Americans had traditionally supported the Republican Party because of its anti-slavery civil rights policies.

Following the passage of the ___E:Civil Rights Act of 1964 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_Rights_Act_of_1964)___ and ___E:Voting Rights Act of 1965 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voting_Rights_Act_of_1965)___ , the Southern states became more reliably Republican in presidential politics, while Northeastern states became more reliably Democratic.

Studies show that Southern whites, which were a core constituency in the Democratic Party, shifted to the Republican Party due to ___E:racial backlash U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_backlash)___ and ___E:social conservatism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_conservatism)___ .
The election of President ___E:John F. Kennedy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy)___ from Massachusetts in 1960 partially reflected this shift.
In the campaign, Kennedy attracted a new generation of younger voters.

In his agenda dubbed the ___E:New Frontier U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Frontier)___ , Kennedy introduced a host of social programs and public works projects, along with enhanced support of the ___E:space program U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA)___ , proposing a crewed spacecraft ___E:trip to the moon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11)___ by the end of the decade.

He pushed for civil rights initiatives and proposed the ___E:Civil Rights Act of 1964 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_Rights_Act_of_1964)___ , but with his ___E:assassination U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_John_F._Kennedy)___ in November 1963, he was not able to see its passage.

Kennedy's successor ___E:Lyndon B. Johnson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyndon_B._Johnson)___ was able to persuade the largely conservative Congress to pass the Civil Rights Act of 1964, and with a more progressive Congress in 1965 passed much of the ___E:Great Society U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Society)___ , including ___E:Medicare U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medicare_(United_States))___ and ___E:Medicaid U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medicaid)___ , which consisted of an array of social programs designed to help the poor, sick, and elderly.

Kennedy and Johnson's advocacy of civil rights further solidified black support for the Democrats but had the effect of alienating Southern whites who would eventually gravitate toward the Republican Party, particularly after the election of ___E:Ronald Reagan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan)___ to the presidency in 1980. Many conservative ___E:Southern Democrats U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Democrats)___ defected to the ___E:Republican Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States))___ , beginning with the passage of the ___E:Civil Rights Act of 1964 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_Rights_Act_of_1964)___ and the general leftward shift of the party.
